messages.ui.about.description:
A sing-box based Xboard proxy client.
The core is distributed as an official prebuilt binary; this program verifies and updates it.

messages.ui.options.from_service: These are the service's current options; changes are written back to the service immediately.
messages.ui.options.groups_readonly: Proxy groups are not editable here yet; this shows the definitions currently in effect. Use the config file to change them.
messages.ui.options.rules_readonly: Rule order is priority, so this screen does not edit them to avoid accidental reordering; this shows the order currently in effect.
messages.ui.options.final_action_note: Used when no rule matches. The default is proxy: falling back to direct silently leaks real traffic whenever a rule fails to cover it.
messages.ui.options.dns_filter_note: These domains never receive a fake address. LAN discovery, time sync and WeChat/QQ callbacks must be listed, otherwise they cannot connect, and the symptom is "some apps mysteriously fail to open".
messages.ui.options.dns_ipv6_note: Off by default: most proxy paths handle IPv6 incompletely, and the symptom is "some sites are slow or time out", which is hard to connect to IPv6.
messages.ui.options.allow_lan_note: When enabled, anyone on the same network can use this proxy as their egress. On public Wi-Fi that means sharing your own traffic exit.
messages.ui.options.tun_strict_note: Off by default: when enabled some applications can resolve but cannot connect, which is expensive to diagnose.
messages.ui.options.tun_dns_address_note: Accepts IPs only, no port: the core's field is an address, and a port makes it reject the config.
messages.ui.options.per_app_desktop_note: Per-app proxying is only meaningful on Android: the desktop system proxy and TUN are both machine-wide.
messages.ui.options.sniff_override_note: Off by default: it makes the real destination differ from the domain the user sees, which misleads diagnosis.
messages.ui.options.sniff_protocols_note: Note: in sing-box the protocol list belongs to a route action, not to an inbound field, and it is not generated yet in this version. Ticking these has no effect; only sniffing itself is enabled.
messages.ui.options.sub_url_note: Normally issued by the panel; fill it in manually only to import a third-party subscription. The URL is itself a credential and is never written to logs.
messages.ui.options.sub_via_proxy_note: On by default: the panel itself sometimes needs a proxy to reach, and turning this off can make every auto-update fail.
messages.ui.options.app_auto_start_note: Starting the app is not the same as taking over the network; ticking this does not make the proxy active.
messages.ui.options.app_log_level: Log level (trace / debug / info / warn / error)
messages.ui.options.app_log_buffer_note: Kept in the UI only, never written to disk: writing logs to disk leaves credentials on disk.
